decisions.quote: The present study replicated the classic Goodman (1965) study, which found that children's reading accuracy improved 60%-80 % in context, in comparison with a list. In the 1st experiment, 100 children read words in context, then in lists. In the 2nd experiment, 97 children read words in lists, then in context (the testing order used in the classic study).
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state files exist for this work. Only the abstract is available in the source file, with no reference list or full text. While the abstract states that it replicated 'the classic Goodman (1965) study' without giving its title or publication venue, shipped row 2310 already records Goodman (1964), 'A LINGUISTIC STUDY OF CUES AND MISCUES IN READING.' (https://www.jstor.org/stable/41387554). Without the reference list or full text, the supplied evidence cannot establish the full bibliographic identity of Goodman (1965) or resolve whether Goodman (1965) and shipped row 2310 (Goodman, 1964) represent the same classic study/work (via a 1964/1965 year discrepancy or alternate report of the same study) versus distinct empirical studies.
